harper: Quick alert 1: post-merge of kernel-routing v2 we see host-side ingress overhead on small prompt traffic. Dropping notes here.

harper: baseline small-chat p50/p95 host-parse: 95ms / 190ms
harper: v2 canary small-chat p50/p95 host-parse: 120ms / 360ms :sweat_smile:

harper: perf sample delta:
```
tokenizer_tokenize     10% -> 28%
memcpy                 3%  -> 16%
grpc_frame_read        6%  -> 11%
kv_cache_lookup        7%  -> 6%
```

rui: That tokenizer + memcpy jump suggests we added a linearize path pre-batch. Which change did v2 introduce?

preethi: v2 adds a kernel rule: prefer "packed_fast" if estimated batch density > 0.6. To estimate density we pre-combine fragments into a probe buffer to measure contiguous size which triggers a memcpy+temp-alloc.

harper: So we do an extra combination per request to decide kernel path. For chat-short that's wasted work because batcher will merge later.

sam: Two fixes: (A) move density estimation after batching (post-merge) so we only probe once per batch, (B) implement a per-worker scratch buffer pool to avoid heap allocs on the probe. Both can be feature flagged.

rui: Short-term rollback? Ops-bot: rolling back kernel-routing v2 on canary now.

ops-bot: canary rollback started at 09:12 UTC. Monitoring streams: ingress-host CPU, small-chat p95, allocs/sec.

preethi: Also worry about KV cache key drift: if we normalize bytes for the probe and then kvcache keys rely on raw fragments, we may change addresses and hashes. Add tag kvcache_key_mode={raw,normalized,probe} and telemetry kernel_probe=true/false.

harper: Good call. Add metric preparse_probe=true/false and probe_reuse_rate.

rui: For the sticky pool idea: implement a ring of fixed-size buffers per-worker (e.g., 8 slots x 8KB). On probe, try to claim slot, write into scratch, mark reused. Avoids malloc/memset churn.

sam: Post-batch selection approach: delay kernel decision until after batch merge. We can attach per-request fragment descriptors to the batch meta so a kernel that supports scatter can be chosen without copying. That's longer work but eliminates the probe.

preethi: Agreed. Long-term: add fragmented-iov-compatible kernel (RTX-5200). Short-term: land scratch-pool (RTX-5197) + move probe post-batch experiment (RTX-5198).

harper: Ops-bot update: rollback complete at 09:17. Canary metrics returning to baseline.

ops-bot: post-rollback quick metrics:
- host-parse p95 back to 198ms
- memcpy portion dropped to ~3% in perf sample
- allocs/sec down 88% from bad canary

rui: Good. Let's run microbench suite: replay 20m small-chat trace with variants: baseline, v2-probe-with-pool, v2-postbatch, v2-pool+postbatch. Collect p50/p95, syscall count, memcpy time, allocs/sec, kvcache hit-rate.

sam: Also instrument grpc writev/readv counts and add ingress-coalesce experiment: coalesce small frames up to 4KB before syscall to reduce syscall tail. Prototype flag: ingress.coalesce=true.

preethi: I'll add telemetry fields: kernel_selection_phase={prebatch,postbatch}, scratch_pool_hit=true/false, ingress_coalesce=true/false, grpc_syscall_count, probe_allocs.

harper: If scratch pool experiment looks good and keeps kvcache stable, we'll canary it at 5% then 25%. Postbatch selection + kernel-iov is the end-state but needs more kernel work and careful perf testing.

rui: One more catch: ensure probe doesn't change canonicalization used by our rerankers/embeddings keys. If we trim whitespace or normalize utf8 during probe we must do same for kvcache keys. Keep probe as a pure memory-copy only.

ops-bot: microbench job queued: job/rt-small-chat-replay-320555-1. Results expected in ~40m.

preethi: I'll push a sticky-pool PR behind flag and a smallbench script and ping this thread with results.

sam: Thanks team. Fast detection + rollback. Keep notes in RTX-5197/5198/5200.
